image_prompt.text: A chain of platforms winding up the outside of a single tower, spaced within jump limits — the ordered route from the base to the top
Platforms on the ascent that vanish after being stepped on or a set time after activation
Trusses, ladders and wall scrambles linking the tower's sections vertically
A reward platform at the summit of the tower

layout_placement.text: The end-of-run payoff placed at the top of the tower — tools, morphs or interactables for players who finish the climb

notes: Prompt is three words. 'tower' matched the index (Obby & Platformer, 'tower climb'); 'avatar' was not resolvable — it could be the Avatar film/series as a theme reference, a character-customisation game (Roleplay & Avatar Sim), or merely the Roblox word for the player character. Classified on 'tower' alone and left 'avatar' as an open question.
Whole Tower Obby preset taken; four of the four options in the handoff are preset-derived, none traceable to the prompt.
Run end inferred from genre rather than asked: an obby ends at the top, emitted as winner-zone.
shape.type and shape.name emitted null — the genre file names typical shapes by ID only, and the Type (Flavor Name) they are split from lives in shapes.md, which step 2 says not to load by default.

open_questions.ask: When you say "avatar tower", which do you mean — a climbing tower themed after Avatar (the film or the series), a tower where players customise their character, or just a plain Roblox obby tower with no reference attached?
On the way up, should players fall all the way back to the bottom, or land on checkpoint pads part-way up the tower?
Nothing was said about how the tower should look — bright and cartoony, neon sci-fi, stone-and-torch fantasy, or grimy industrial?

skill_gap.name: no handling for an unresolved reference word
skill_gap.why: Half the content of this prompt is the word "avatar", which is simultaneously a genre name in the index (Roleplay & Avatar Sim), a plausible IP theme reference, and the ordinary Roblox word for the player character. The skill's only instruction for a term it cannot parse is to ask, so with no human the load-bearing half of a two-word prompt is resolved by a guess with nothing in the handoff marking that it was one — notes is the only place it lands, and notes is addressed to the pipeline rather than to whoever would correct it.

notes_for_us: 'avatar' and 'tower' each hit the index (Roleplay & Avatar Sim; Obby's 'tower climb'), and the only tie-break offered is 'the dominant genre is the one the sentence is about' — which for a bare two-word noun phrase is a grammar call, not a rule.

Emit requires shape.type and shape.name split from the shape row's Type (Flavor Name), but genre files list typical shapes as bare IDs and step 2 forbids loading shapes.md by default — the two fields are unfillable without breaking the read rule.

Nothing caps how much a preset may supply on a near-empty prompt: three words produced four options, so the whole handoff is preset-derived while 'never inject an option the user did not choose' is nominally satisfied.

Theme is required to be null-plus-a-question when the prompt is silent, but there is no guidance for a proper noun that might BE the theme — 'avatar' may be the answer to the theme question rather than a gap in it.

'terse-reference' prompts have no route for the reference itself: if 'avatar' is an IP, nothing in the handoff can carry 'looks like Pandora' except free text in theme, and the skill never says whether naming a franchise is allowed there.
